Kraken co-CEO Arjun Sethi calls going public in the US the slowest piece of financial plumbing left

"Going public in the United States is expensive. It is the slowest piece of financial plumbing left."

"I'm living it, and so are my portfolio companies."

"What I've seen up close from the founder side, sitting on the boards of companies and investing in them is time. The process is measured in quarters and years, not weeks."

"Audits, controls, filings, every number defined and then redefined and then restructured. Every metric then is argued over with people who have never run your business in any capacity."

"Frankly, they learn more on your dime than they can give you advice for."

Premise: 

Incentives drive all human behavior. 

The corollary: 

How to destroy a country:

A vast social security and support system that serves as a magnet for those who would rather not work.

An open immigration policy that does not screen immigrants to determine their ability and willingness to provide for themselves and their families. 

An open immigration policy that does not screen for political and/or religious ideologies that are a threat to the country. 

Economic incentives large enough to incentivize immigrants on the state dole to have large numbers of children, but insufficient for educated and economically productive mothers to be able to quit to raise a family. 

The declining fertility of the most educated and productive women due to their delay to begin a family as a result of their desire and/or need to advance their careers, among other reasons, to live a life they deem consistent with their educational achievements and/or to repay their student debts. 

Amnesty programs that give citizenship  and voting power to illegal immigrants without consideration of their economic productivity or their threat to the country due to their religious or political ideologies. 

The changing demographics and increased population due to the above factors. 

The state responding to protests by increasing social support. 

The continued failure to punish and hold accountable violent and looting rioters. 

Government managed by a massive and growing unelected bureaucracy.

text:
This is the new Tesla Roadster's fan and suction system, which the company filed a patent for in April 2025.

Sides skirts and front and rear skirts deploy under the battery pack, sucking the car down at ~2G. Because the skirts can move, they have some compliance, so they can deal with road bumps, road debris, etc. As the speed of the Roadster increases, the front and rear skirts retract to allow for air-flow (venturi effect) under the vehicle.

Tesla: "Our multi-mode fan and ground sealing system acts as a downforce generator, pulling air out from beneath the vehicle. This provides enough suction to hold the vehicle upside down, even when stationary. Powered fans and active wings maximize traction and cornering speeds in all conditions, achieving massive downforce at zero speed."

In their patent, Tesla said: "In the first mode, a complete set of skirts creates a fully sealed bounded region under the vehicle with central fans generating maximum downforce at low speeds on smooth surfaces. In the second mode, a subset of skirts (primarily side skirts) modifies the bounded region while all fans operate to provide downforce in dynamic driving conditions with uneven surfaces. The system includes a control mechanism to selectively deploy skirts and operate fans based on driving conditions, optimizing between maximum downforce at low speeds and improved performance over varying terrain at higher speeds."

Some impressions from the Bank-Fund meetings in Bangkok:

1. The words are all negative but the numbers are all positive. Is all about unprecedented waves of shocks and risks while the IMF upgraded the forecast to something even stronger.

2. No one cares about tariffs anymore, they expect them to continue forever and have adjusted and moved on.

3. Everyone cares a lot about high interest rates. They expect them to continue forever but they haven't moved on.

4. Oil prices fall somewhere between these two. Everyone cares some, aren't sure if they'll continue and have partially moved on.

5. Everyone is having exactly the same conversations about AI as they are having here: will the demand boost continue, is it a bubble, will it kill jobs, when will it show up in productivity. I sensed much more optimism than pessimism and finance ministers and central bankers are not particuarly interested in p(doom).

6. No one seemed to mind that Scott Bessent didn't bother to attend.

text:
Trying out the new Meta glasses from Thailand. Today’s topic is the Tesla flying car. I look at it from multiple perspectives. From just permitting, there’s a lot of challenges. What’s so interesting about it, the technology itself is getting there and I think for metropolitan areas it’s gonna be very difficult. For long-haul traffic it could be very cool. Or in rural areas, even better, flying around in your car. I love the idea. 

From a perspective of investing, here’s what I think is going to happen. I think there’s no question that Tesla’s going to merge with SpaceX because that technology is coming together like this. So if you own Tesla stock, you’re going to own New Co. If you already own SpaceX, hang in. You’re going to own Tesla. It’s going to happen that way. #shotonmeta #metaglasses
